title: Program Planning / SDLC
subtitle: Before writing a single line of code, professional developers follow a structured process called the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC). The 2024/2025 exam asked directly for the 6 SDLC steps (Q1b, 5 marks). Know them in order.
learningOutcome: Before writing a single line of code, professional developers follow a structured process called the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC). The 2024/2025 exam asked directly for the 6 SDLC steps (Q1b, 5 marks). Know them in order.

content.text: Step 1 — Feasibility Study Inspect how viable and achievable the project is. Check availability of requirements, resources, and personnel. Is the project worth doing?
Step 2 — System Design Create a systematic design/blueprint after the feasibility study. This includes data structures, interfaces, and algorithms before any code is written.
Step 3 — Implementation (Coding) The actual coding phase. Developers write code based on the design document. This is where Python programs are written.

Step 4 — Testing Test the code to find errors/bugs. Three types: Unit Testing (test individual components), Integration Testing (test components working together), User-Interface Testing (test from the user's perspective).
Step 5 — Deployment Release the code to the client. The developer must ensure the code is flexible, documented, and ready for use in the real environment.
Step 6 — Maintenance Annual or periodic checks on the program to protect, maintain, and improve it. Bug fixes, updates, and security patches.

Exam answer — write this verbatim:
The SDLC consists of 6 steps: (1) Feasibility Study — assess viability; (2) System Design — create a blueprint; (3) Implementation — write the code; (4) Testing — find and fix bugs; (5) Deployment — release to client; (6) Maintenance — ongoing support and improvement.

items: • Briefly explain the steps involved in the software development life cycle. 2024/2025 Q1b — 5 marks
• What is the difference between unit testing and integration testing?
• What is pseudocode? Write pseudocode for a program that finds the larger of two numbers.

questions.question: State the textbook definition — Exam answer — write this verbatim.
questions.answer: The SDLC consists of 6 steps: (1) Feasibility Study — assess viability; (2) System Design — create a blueprint; (3) Implementation — write the code; (4) Testing — find and fix bugs; (5) Deployment — release to client; (6) Maintenance — ongoing support and improvement.

content.text: Pseudocode is plain-English description of an algorithm — not actual Python syntax, but structured enough to be converted to code easily.
Example — Find the larger of two numbers
START INPUT number_a INPUT number_b IF number_a > number_b THEN OUTPUT "number_a is larger" ELSE OUTPUT "number_b is larger" END

Common mistake — Listing only 4 or 5 SDLC steps — the full list is 6. Testing (step 4) is the one most students forget to split into unit/integration/UI. Also: confusing Deployment (release to client) with Maintenance (ongoing support after release).
